items.title: 52220_Woody Herman oral history interview
items.q: the very first person out of Duke's band that came with us had already left the band, and that was Juan Tizol.

ctx.x: first connected-- members of the Ellington organization, Johnny and Ben and --

Well, it was just because they knew what we were into, and they felt the band was trying something. And whether they agreed that what we were doing was the greatest or not, but they also knew that there was some bread to be gotten, plus the fact that they wouldn't be asked to do something that was foreign to their nature musically. So I think it worked out very well. As a matter of fact, the very first person out of Duke's band that came with us had already left the band, and that was Juan Tizol. And he was the…

items.title: 61531_Juan Tizol oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...lists an H. Lenk. Do you know an H. Lenk? Did he have anything to do with Perdido or the lyrics? [INTERVIEWEE] Lenk?

ctx.x: And he is the only one who ever wrote lyrics. And then you showed me a 78 record of Woody Herman and the New Third Herd recording of Perdido, and on that record, the composer credits, in addition to yourself and Ervin Drake, lists an H. Lenk. Do you know an H. Lenk? Did he have anything to do with Perdido or the lyrics?
